- `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for the consumer API. Every module is `pub` today because the library API is not designed yet, so none of it is stable before 1.0. `[convention]`
- No wildcard `_` arm on enums this crate owns; a compile error on a new variant is the point. Clippy cannot scope this lint to owned enums, so it is not enabled. `[convention]`
- Code never cites spec, criterion or plan IDs (`SPEC-001`, `AC-007`, `T-009`). Specs change; the code says what it guarantees in its own words, and tests name the behavior they prove. `[convention]`

## Testing

- `cargo nextest` plus `cargo test --doc`. `insta` for snapshots: accept a snapshot change only after confirming the new output is correct, not just different.
- Assert content, not presence: `assert_eq!` on the exact value over `contains`/`is_some`.
- Sibling-path parity: a function that mirrors an already-tested one gets a test asserting the same contract.
- CI gates line coverage; the threshold is the `coverage` recipe's default in the justfile.

## Plugins

Start work through these commands so their checks run:

- Options before deciding: `/guide:explore`. Does it work: `/guide:spike`.
- Bug or review findings: `/guide:fix`. Real feature or shared change: `/guide:build`.
- Verify or find bugs: `/guide:check`. Commit: `/guide:ship`.

Changesets follow the convention in `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Writing a changeset").

Pull requests are opened by Entire from the branch's trail: push the branch and create or link its trail (`entire trail create`). Do not open the PR with `gh`.

## Fixing bugs

Look for structurally identical siblings and fix them in the same change. If one is deliberately left, say where and why.

A change is done when:

- CI has passed on the PR. Until it has run, say it is pending.
- Docs, comments, tests and dead code that described the old behavior are updated or removed.
- A test guards the change and fails without it.
- Nothing is skipped, dropped or defaulted without a count or a message.
- Claims in the PR, docs and comments hold for the current code. Anything taken from another agent or an earlier run is rechecked or marked unverified.

## Facts a reviewer should know

- Supported platforms are macOS and Linux. There is no Windows target.
- The crate is pre-1.0: a minor bump may break the public API. The changeset's bump says which.
- A release happens when the Callisto release PR merges. `Cargo.toml` can be ahead of what is published, so check crates.io or `just verify-release <version>` before calling something released.
- Designs in `docs/spec/` and `docs/architecture/` are plans unless the code has them. `README.md` describes what works today.

When the spec itself is wrong, fix the spec file and add an entry to [`05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md) explaining what was wrong and why the fix is right. A decision that departs from the spec with a credible alternative gets an ADR.

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md).
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions.
- Comments explain only the non-obvious why, carry no history (the commit records it), and fill to 120 columns.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why. Skip the body when the subject says it all.

- `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for the consumer API. Every module is `pub` today because the library API is not designed yet, so none of it is stable before 1.0. `[convention]`
- No wildcard `_` arm on enums this crate owns; a compile error on a new variant is the point. Clippy cannot scope this lint to owned enums, so it is not enabled. `[convention]`
- Code never cites spec, criterion or plan IDs (`SPEC-001`, `AC-007`, `T-009`). Specs change; the code says what it guarantees in its own words, and tests name the behavior they prove. `[convention]`

## Testing

- `cargo nextest` plus `cargo test --doc`. `insta` for snapshots: accept a snapshot change only after confirming the new output is correct, not just different.
- Assert content, not presence: `assert_eq!` on the exact value over `contains`/`is_some`.
- Sibling-path parity: a function that mirrors an already-tested one gets a test asserting the same contract.
- CI gates line coverage; the threshold is the `coverage` recipe's default in the justfile.

## Plugins

Start work through these commands so their checks run:

- Options before deciding: `/guide:explore`. Does it work: `/guide:spike`.
- Bug or review findings: `/guide:fix`. Real feature or shared change: `/guide:build`.
- Verify or find bugs: `/guide:check`. Commit: `/guide:ship`.

Changesets follow the convention in `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Writing a changeset").

Pull requests are opened by Entire from the branch's trail: push the branch and create or link its trail (`entire trail create`). Do not open the PR with `gh`.

## Fixing bugs

Look for structurally identical siblings and fix them in the same change. If one is deliberately left, say where and why.

A change is done when:

- CI has passed on the PR. Until it has run, say it is pending.
- Docs, comments, tests and dead code that described the old behavior are updated or removed.
- A test guards the change and fails without it.
- Nothing is skipped, dropped or defaulted without a count or a message.
- Claims in the PR, docs and comments hold for the current code. Anything taken from another agent or an earlier run is rechecked or marked unverified.

## Facts a reviewer should know

- Supported platforms are macOS and Linux. There is no Windows target.
- The crate is pre-1.0: a minor bump may break the public API. The changeset's bump says which.
- A release happens when the Callisto release PR merges. `Cargo.toml` can be ahead of what is published, so check crates.io or `just verify-release <version>` before calling something released.
- Designs in `docs/spec/` and `docs/architecture/` are plans unless the code has them. `README.md` describes what works today.

When the spec itself is wrong, fix the spec file and add an entry to [`05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md) explaining what was wrong and why the fix is right. A decision that departs from the spec with a credible alternative gets an ADR.

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md).
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions.
- Comments explain only the non-obvious why, carry no history (the commit records it), and fill to 120 columns.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why. Skip the body when the subject says it all.
